newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: St Barbara Mines CEO resigned - director.
newsitem.headline: St Barbara Mines CEO resigned - director.

text.p: St Barbara Mines Ltd director Ross Atkins said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange on Tuesday that St Barbara's chief executive Robin Dean resigned as chief executive on April 3.
Atkins said Dean resigned because he said he could not work effectively with Atkins if Atkins was re-elected to the board of St Barbara at an extraordinary general meeting on April 3.
Atkins said after his re-election, other directors of St Barbara, Norman Bevan, Peter Jones and Leslie Nixon, then offered to Dean that he withdraw his resignation without the approval of the board.
"The conduct of Messrs Jones, Bevan and Nixon in offering re-employment to Messrs Dean and Roberts, did not constitute a valid resolution of the directors of St Barbara Mines," Atkins said.

"As a director of St Barbara Mines Ltd, I am advising shareholders that I propose to take stwps to have the above course of conduct of the current directors, its former chief executive and its former company secretary fully investigated and to ensure, in future, that the shareholders are fully informed of signficiant events in relation to the company," Atkins said.

Atkins, who jointly controls 47.2 percent of St Barbara with former chairman Alan Birchmore, opposes St Barbara's takeover offer for Mt Leyshon Mines Ltd of 32 St Barbara shares for every 10 Mt Leyshon Mines.
Mt Leyshon has advised shareholders to reject the bid.
Atkins said company secretary Neil Roberts had also resigned and had been re-offered his position by Jones, Bevan and Nixon after a meeting of directors Atkins did not know about.
St Barbara Mines' shares closed down four cents at 62 cents on Monday, while Mt Leyshon's shares closed one cent firmer at A$1.96 on Monday. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
